title: Outlook: new settings to block or load external images
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap's promised settings from the surrounding product documentation. The licensing statements are supported, and targeted searches found no documented admin allowance or initial state for the new controls.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft's Outlook deployment guidance describes junk senders placing web beacons with external content such as graphic images in HTML email.
claims.quote: Junk email senders often add a web beacon in HTML email messages that includes external content, such as graphic images.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: That guidance says opening or viewing the email lets the web beacon verify that the recipient's address is valid.
claims.quote: When users open or view the email, the web beacons verify that their email addresses are valid.

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy has an ExternalImageProxyEnabled parameter controlling whether external images load through the Outlook external image proxy.
claims.quote: The ExternalImageProxyEnabled parameter specifies whether to load all external images through the Outlook external image proxy. Valid values are:

claims.claim: ExternalImageProxyEnabled is not described as the control for blocking external content or allowing load-all by default.
claims.quote:
$true: All external images are loaded through the Outlook external image proxy. This value is the default.
- $false: All external images are loaded through the web browser.

claims.claim: By default, users can configure their own safelist collection in Outlook or Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: By default, users can configure the safelist collection on their own mailboxes in Outlook or Outlook on the web.

claims.claim: Admins can use Set-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration to configure the safelist collection on a user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Admins can use the corresponding parameters on the Set-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration cmdlet to configure the safelist collection on a user's mailbox.

claims.claim: Under the roadmap's stated default, whether a sender is safe determines whether its external content loads.
claims.quote: Existing default behavior will not be changed (load external content only for safe senders).

claims.claim: The roadmap text describes no change to sign-in, roles or identity.
claims.quote: New settings will allow customers to block all external content, or to load all content by default if the customer admin allows.
